narration: The Sound of the Andes: Kantu
This is Kantu. Pre-Columbian to present.
on_screen: Title card: Kantu · Bolivia, Peru · Pre-Columbian to present

scenes.title: Where and when
narration: Kantu is a pre-Columbian tradition originating from the Mollo culture, with its historical center in Charazani, Bolivia.
It has been practiced in the Peruvian and Bolivian highlands since the pre-Incaic epoch.

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: The origins of the dance are considered ceremonial.
It is currently practiced by Quechua communities in Charazani.
Today it is a living tradition.

scenes.title: Watch it
on_screen: Formation: Circle dance with optional pairs inside or outside the circle.
scenes.music: diegetic (the video's own sound), underscore under narration

scenes.title: Listen
narration: The music is performed by bands of sicuris using the siku, a ceremonial panpipe.
It is characterized by the use of parallel fifths and fourths, achieved by using the same fingering on instruments tuned to intervals of fifths and octaves.
Characterized by the sound of sicu bands playing in parallel fifths and fourths, creating a distinct, layered harmonic texture.

scenes.title: The people
narration: Notable ensembles include Los Kjarkas, Inkuyo, Bolivia Manta, Grupo Aymara, Awatiñas, Markasata, and the K'antu Ensemble.
It is a subclass of Andean music and indigenous American dance, with roots in the Mollo culture.
